title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

reports.title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

summary:
Angela Lipps, 50, of Tennessee is suing Fargo, North Dakota and police detective Lucas Heck for $10 million after being falsely arrested and jailed for about six months. She was taken at gunpoint from her home in July 2025 while babysitting four children, held nearly four months in a Tennessee jail awaiting extradition, then about two more months in North Dakota on theft and identity fraud charges. The charges were dropped after her lawyer supplied bank records showing she was in Tennessee when the Fargo fraud occurred, and she was released on Christmas Eve.

The lawsuit says a West Fargo investigator used AI facial recognition on a fake ID from surveillance video, and it returned Lipps's social media photo as a possible match. Detective Heck allegedly relied on that lead without further investigation or probable cause. Lipps says she lost her home, car, and belongings, was denied medications and dentures, and suffered lasting trauma. Fargo officials declined to comment on the pending litigation.
